versions.short: The bill would direct the Secretary of the Interior, working with the Western Dakota Regional Water System, Inc., to study whether a proposed project to bring water from the Missouri River to western South Dakota is feasible. After the study, the Secretary would prepare a report with a recommendation on whether the project is technically and financially feasible, whether it should be authorized for construction, and what share of construction costs the non-federal side should pay, which would be at least 25 percent. The report would be sent to the Senate and House committees on natural resources and made public. The federal government would cover up to half of the study's cost, with total federal spending on the study capped at $10,000,000, and the study authority would expire five years after enactment.
